It was decided to install an Enpack drain at one location. During
the installation in borehole H5, the procedures required to form the
impermeable invert were demonstrated to be complicated, and doubt was
expressed over the likely success of forming such an invert under site
conditions. The difficulties were further aggravated by the fact that
water was flowing from the hole fairly rapidly during installation. This
particular installation is discussed in more detail later. Because of the
installation difficulties experienced with the 'Enpack drain' and the
limited benefit of such a drain in intercepting infiltrating groundwater,
this design was abandoned.

An alternative type of drain was used which took the form of a screen
installed below the water table at the end of an unperforated section of
pipe. Because of significant water flow around the oborehole/drain
annulus, attempts were made to grout the annulus up to the screen. Such a
drain can only lower the water taple into whicn the screen is placed but,
1f successfully grouted, does prevent the water from seeping back into the
slope nearer the slope face (Figure 9).

It was originally envisaged tnat the choice of screen type would be a
critical factor in drain design if a loss of fines througn the drain
openings was to be avoided. The grading curves obtained for samples taken
from vertical boreholes at Po Shan showed a wide even soil grading for all
completely decomposed volcanic rock, including inter-corestone material.
Tne fine material led to the adoption of a composite filter of sand and
Terran 1000 fabric for the pumping well used for a pumping test carried
out at Po Shan. Because the placement of such a filter in a horizontal
drain is extremely difficult, it was decided to install drains with a
filter formed of Terram 1000 alone. This was fixed to a 50 mm diameter
PVC pipe, which was perforated with five rows of 7.5 mn diameter noles,
using a contact adhesive (Plate 12). This type of drain liner was used
for horizontal drains H3A, H4 and H5. wo loss of fines througn these
holes was noted.

Because of concern over the long-term performance of the filter
fabric with respect to clogging, alternative designs of screen were used
in the other holes. The first of these was made from 50 mm nominal
diameter (ND) PVC pipe with a wall thickness of 4.5 mm. This was slotted
with 1 mn wide slots at 12 mm centres extending to the diameter (Plate
13). The slotting reduced the rigidity of this pipe to sucn an extent
tnat these drain liners broke during installation, and none could be
successtully installed. A close copy of tnis type of screen was
manufactured from 40 mn ND galvanized iron pipe. The slots in this were
tormed sy sawing with a hack-saw, and were approximately 1.5 mn wide
{Plate 14). Drain liners of this type were used in drainage holes H8 and
Ho, tne latter installation peing re-galvanized electrolytically after
slotting. These screens showed clear water flow within six hours of
installation, indicating that an adequate filter pack nad formed over tne
slots.
